question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{1-x/3},\, & x\ge 3 \\ 0,\, & x<3\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<3 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 3\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x\ge 3,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<3 \\ {\int }_{3}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 3\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{3}^{x}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{1-t/3}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-{e}^{1-t/3}{|}_{3}^{x} \\  & =-{e}^{1-x/3}+1 \\  & =1-{e}^{1-x/3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<3, \\ 1-{e}^{1-x/3}, & x\ge 3.\end{aligned}
$$
